label: John 13:3
text: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came from God, and was going to God,

text: Then he came to Simon Peter. He said to him, “Lord, do you wash my feet?”

text:

“You don’t know what I am doing now, but you will understand later.”

text:

label: John 13:9
text: Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!”

label: John 13:10
text:
Jesus said to him,
“Someone who has bathed only needs to have his feet washed, but is completely clean. You are clean, but not all of you.”

label: John 13:11
text:
For he knew him who would betray him, therefore he said,
“You are not all clean.”

label: John 13:12
text:
So when he had washed their feet, put his outer garment back on, and sat down again, he said to them,
“Do you know what I have done to you?

label: John 13:13
text: You call me, ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord.’ You say so correctly, for so I am.

label: John 13:14
text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.

label: John 13:15
text: For I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.

label: John 13:16
text: Most certainly I tell you, a servant is not greater than his lord, neither one who is sent greater than he who sent him.

label: John 13:17
text: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.

label: John 13:18
text: I don’t speak concerning all of you. I know whom I have chosen. But that the Scripture may be fulfilled, ‘He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.’

label: John 13:19
text: From now on, I tell you before it happens, that when it happens, you may believe that I am he.

label: John 13:20

label: John 13:21
text:
When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in spirit, and testified,

label: John 13:22
text: The disciples looked at one another, perplexed about whom he spoke.

label: John 13:23
text: One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was at the table, leaning against Jesus’ breast.

After the piece of bread, then Satan entered into him.

text:

Jesus answered him,
“Will you lay down your life for me? Most certainly I tell you, the rooster won’t crow until you have denied me three times.

label: The last supper took place before the feast of the Passover
statement: John dates the last supper 'Now before the feast of the Passover' (13:1); in John 18:28 the leaders avoid the praetorium 'so they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover'. In John's chronology this farewell supper is not the Passover seder, unlike the Synoptic Passover meal.

label: Jesus washed the disciples' feet during supper
statement: Jesus arose from supper, laid aside his garments, girded himself with a towel, poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet and to wipe them with the towel - a task elsewhere the work of a servant or of the host's lowest slave.

label: One who has bathed needs only his feet washed
statement: Jesus said 'Someone who has bathed only needs to have his feet washed, but is completely clean' - presupposing a bath before the feast and feet soiled on the walk, washed at arrival.

label: Jesus quoted Psalm 41:9 of his betrayer
statement: Jesus applied scripture to the betrayal: 'He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me' (Psalm 41:9) - 'that the Scripture may be fulfilled'.

label: Jesus testified during supper that one of the disciples would betray him
statement: Troubled in spirit, Jesus testified 'Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me', and the disciples looked at one another, perplexed about whom he spoke.

label: The beloved disciple reclined against Jesus's breast at the table
statement: One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was 'at the table, leaning against Jesus' breast' (en to kolpo), and 'leaning back, as he was, on Jesus' breast' asked who the betrayer was - the reclining posture of a Judean festive meal.

label: Jesus dipped a morsel in the dish and gave it to Judas
statement: Jesus answered, 'It is he to whom I will give this piece of bread when I have dipped it'; he dipped the morsel (psomion) and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot - dipping bread in a shared dish at a meal.

label: Satan entered Judas after the morsel; the devil had already put it into his heart
statement: John 13:2 says 'the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him'; after the morsel 'Satan entered into him' (13:27) and Jesus said 'What you do, do quickly'.

label: Judas held the disciples' money box (glossokomon)
statement: Some thought, because Judas had the money box (glossokomon), that Jesus said 'Buy what things we need for the feast' or that he should give something to the poor - a common fund for the group's needs and alms.
